title: a-measured-seal-is-never-replaced-by-an-unrequested-one
from_idea: none, because this entered by the TICKET door: it is a bug, and editing lines of code fixes it (the /intent skill's own rule). It was uncovered by voyage 1c4ae8f053fe, whose ruling attaches such a defect to the uncovering voyage — but that voyage is PROVED and closed, so it cannot attach and is cast here instead.

intention: The tester's write door refuses to replace a seal that was ASKED FOR with one that was NOT — and a re-seal reproduces the isolation the standing seal was taken at, rather than silently falling back to the default.
why:
MEASURED 2026-09-08, and it is how the defect was found: re-sealing a batch with `cairn test --seal` and no `--netns` replaced `seal: {verdict: sealed, detail: '1.1.1.1:53 reachable bare, unreachable inside netns'}` with `seal: {verdict: open, detail: 'none: no seal requested'}` across 44 validations. Nothing refused it, nothing announced it, and it was caught only by diffing test_diagnostic.json BY HAND. The corpus was restored by re-running with --netns and is clean today (measured: 201 validation files against 25 revisions, 125 high-water marks, ZERO standing downgrades) — so this ticket is the physics, not a repair.

THE AXIS IS NOT STRENGTH, IT IS WHETHER ANYONE LOOKED, and isolation.py's own comments already draw the line: SEALED is 'asked for, confirmed from inside'; INDETERMINATE is 'asked for, could not be confirmed'; BREACHED is 'asked for, the route is STILL there'; OPEN alone is 'NOT asked for'. Three of the four are measurements and must be free to land — a sealed->breached is a measured failure and Law 7 says it lands loudly. Only sealed|indeterminate|breached -> open replaces a measurement with the absence of one, which is Law 3 read backwards: an unmeasured claim taking the place of a measured one.

AND THE HOLLOW GREEN IS THE COST. A validation that reads `seal: open` is not wrong about anything — it accurately says no seal was requested. What it does is quietly retire evidence a peer was leaning on (Law 8: a false green gets leaned on, which is why it is worse here than a red), and it does it at the exact moment a re-seal sweep is claiming to REFRESH the corpus. The sweep's whole purpose is to make the seals current; dropping 44 measurements is the opposite act wearing the same command.
how:
TWO CHANGES, and the second is why the first will not be routed around.

1. THE GUARD, at cairn/devices/tester/validation_store.py::persist_validation — the single write-door. Before `_atomic_write`, compare the standing record's `evidence.seal.verdict` with the incoming one. If the standing verdict is any of sealed|indeterminate|breached and the incoming is `open`, REFUSE. The refusal names both verdicts, the proof, and the one-flag fix (`--netns`). The same predicate covers `evidence.instance_seal` for free (it has no 'not requested' state today, so it never fires there — which is the correct amount of code for a rule that is about the axis, not about one field).

   THE ESCAPE ROUTE IS A RECORDED ACT, NEVER A FLAG THAT SOFTENS THE GATE. A caller that genuinely means to drop the measurement passes `unsealing_because='<reason>'`, and the reason is written into the new record's evidence so a reader a year out sees WHY it was dropped. Silence is refused; a reason is permanent. This is the shape CLAUDE.md names — 'a deterministic red is fixed, or it carries a ruling — never a paragraph', and the ruling requirement is an escape route rather than a lock — and it is NOT the advisory switch ruled out on 2026-09-07: the gate still refuses, it just admits a claim that costs something to make.

2. THE RE-SEAL REPRODUCES ITS OWN ISOLATION. `cairn test --seal` reads the standing validation's `evidence.seal.verdict` per proof and re-runs at the isolation that seal was taken at, rather than at the flagless default. Without this, the guard fires on the ORDINARY path — 121 of 201 validations are sealed, so every bare re-seal of any of them refuses — and a gate that refuses correct intent constantly is a gate people learn to route around. With it, the common path is right by default and the guard only ever meets a caller who is actually dropping a measurement.

WHAT IS OUT: the reseal DOOR of ticket 4d9115eb04cd (a different axis — a seal whose proof no longer REPRODUCES, versus a seal replaced by a non-measurement). This ticket's guard sits UNDERNEATH that door and holds when it is built. Also out: making the network seal default-on, which is a change to what every proof costs and is Akien's call, not a side effect of a bug fix.

falsifier.proves_green: proof gate — cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_seal_is_never_silently_dropped.py (new), teeth under an isolated scratch validations root so no live seal is touched. Sealed by the tester itself (same-hand seal is the ruled exception for code).
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when, against a scratch validations dir: (1) persisting `seal: open` over a standing `seal: sealed` is REFUSED, and the refusal names both verdicts and the --netns fix; (2) the same over standing `indeterminate` and standing `breached` is also refused; (3) sealed -> breached, sealed -> indeterminate, and open -> open all LAND unrefused, because three of the four verdicts are measurements and only their loss is the defect; (4) the refusal is lifted by `unsealing_because='<reason>'` AND the reason is readable in the persisted record afterward — an override that leaves no trace fails this tooth; (5) `cairn test --seal` over a proof whose standing seal is `sealed` re-runs under netns with no flag given, and the resulting record still reads `sealed`. WRONG INTENT if the corpus's ratio of sealed-to-open validations drifts downward over the following weeks — that would mean the guard is being satisfied by passing `unsealing_because` rather than by keeping the seal, and the words landed while the measurement kept leaking.

traces_to: Law 3 — nothing is known until measured, and this is its mirror: a measurement may not be replaced by the absence of one. Law 8 — a hollow green gets leaned on by a peer, so retiring 44 seals inside a command that claims to refresh them is worse than a red. Law 4 — the rule is at the write door, in the kernel, not in a paragraph asking the operator to remember --netns.

watchme.trigger: at each persist_validation that lowers a seal to `open`, and on the corpus census the build gate already walks
watchme.enough: when 30 days pass with zero `unsealing_because` records in the corpus and the sealed:open ratio has not fallen — at that point the guard has met no legitimate downgrade and the escape route can be argued out
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier
watchme.nexus: the tester's own validations dir is the record; the probe reads it
